content:
mike: Heads-up: docusaurus build failed on import branch. Error points to a code fence that contains an HTML comment and a relative image path. Build log: `Error: malformed HTML in fenced code block` then later `Can't resolve fragment: #install-guide` from a moved file.

olivia: I ran it locally. The issue is twofold: our slugify step chokes on `<-- comment -->` inside triple backticks if the fence language is missing; and we moved docs/setup/install.md to docs/getting-started/install.md which left a bunch of relative links pointing to ../setup/install.md.

jen: I opened PR 4578 with a minimal fix: (1) explicit code-fence language for the affected block, (2) update relative links to the new path, and (3) add a small test fixture. It fixes the build but I'm worried about other stray relative links across the repo.

ci-bot: build: branch/pr/4578  build failed (stage). See https://ci.redwood-inference.local/builds/8010

kevin: For broader coverage, can we add a pre-commit linkcheck hook that runs a lightweight subset of linkcheck for changed files? Something quick like `node scripts/changed-link-check.js` that only validates intra-doc fragments and image paths.

olivia: Agree. Also suggest a migration helper `scripts/fix-relpaths.js --rewrite` that scans moved files and rewrites `](../setup/` => `](../getting-started/` when safe. It should run in dry-run by default.

mike: Good call. Jen: please add a short entry in PR 4578 describing the heuristic so reviewers can eyeball rewrites. We don't want to accidentally rewrite intentionally non-migrated vendor links.

jen: Will do. Also added docs-bot comment to the PR with the failing snippets.

docs-bot: NOTE: found 23 changed markdown files with relative links to `../setup/` on branch. Suggested rewrites attached to PR 4578.

ci-bot: linkcheck: after fixes on 4578, staging build shows 3 remaining fragment failures tied to anchors inside `CONTRIBUTING.md` which uses manual HTML anchors (`<a id=...>`). Docusaurus expects heading-generated slugs, so those don't match.

kevin: For the manual anchors, we can add a tiny mapping plugin that reads HTML id attributes and registers them as valid fragments during build. That avoids changing CONTRIBUTING.md and preserves author intent.

olivia: Another approach: normalize by adding explicit heading comments in CONTRIBUTING.md like `<!-- slug: contributing-guidelines -->` and update the build to respect `slug:` comments. Which is cleaner? Plugin vs in-file hints?

mike: Plugin is lower friction for contributors. But add the `<!-- slug: ... -->` option as fallback. Plugin should generate a warning when it auto-maps a manual anchor so authors can opt-in.

jen: I'll update PR 4578 to: a) include `scripts/fix-relpaths.js` dry-run and rewrite; b) add pre-commit changed-link-check hook; c) add plugin scaffold to map manual HTML ids into fragment registry; d) tests for the codefence HTML-comment case.

docs-bot: preview: https://deploy-preview-4578.docs.redwood-inference.com/ (staging)

ci-bot: build: staging/docs (after update)  linkcheck passed for changed files, 0 broken links in PR scope. Full site check scheduled.

mike: Great. After merge, let's run the full repo linkcheck during the next quiet window and then enable the pre-commit hook org-wide.

kevin: Note: pre-commit should be opt-out for external contributors on forks; otherwise their CI will fail. Make the hook advisory in repo README with instructions to run locally or as CI step.

olivia: I'll draft a short post in #docs summarizing the migration helpers and the hook, link to PR 4578, and ask folks to run the tool on any large cleanup PRs.

jen: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4578 (WIP). Thanks for the reviews so far. I'll iterate and re-run full linkcheck.

mike: Thanks everyone. Once merged, remember to notify support and add a blurb to the release notes about corrected anchors and pre-commit guide.
